newsitem.title: USA: Dlr/mark ends at its highest weekly close in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/mark ends at its highest weekly close in 1996.

text.p: The dollar ended higher on Friday, bolstered by European leaders' agreement on a landmark pact on budget discipline and a later-denied rumor that a consultancy report said Japanese officials desire a stronger dollar against the yen, dealers said.

The German mark weakened against the dollar and most other European currencies after a hard-fought Franco-German battle over fiscal discipline standards post European monetary union ended with a signed pact.
The pact takes the 15-nation bloc a major step closer to the goal of a single European currency in 1999.

"The pact is bullish for the dollar with the implication being that Europe is a little closer to agreement on European monetary union, which is basically deutschemark negative," said Steven Walker, senior trader at Skandinaviska Enskilda Banken in New York.
"If it's deutschemark negative, it's got to be dollar positive," he added.

The dollar posted early U.S. gains against the yen on market rumors that a Washington-based consultancy had issued a report saying that Japanese officials would tolerate a higher dollar/yen exchange rate of 120 yen.
However, ensuing news of the European pact spurred dealers to buy yen in order to sell marks, capping the dollar's rise against the Japanese currency.

"The rumor was pushing dollar/yen higher. But at the same time, a lot of people began selling marks for yen, which kept the dollar/yen rate capped," said Peter Ullrich, vice-president of foreign exchange at GiroCredit Bank.

Also buoying the dollar was an exceptionally large purchase of dollars for yen, said to be one billion dollar, by a U.S. money fund, and strong buying by Japanese trust banks, eager to own dollars ahead of their expected participation in next week's auction of two- and five-year U.S. Treasury notes.
The dollar closed higher at 1.5541/46 marks compared to an open of 1.5395/05 marks. Against the yen, the dollar rose to 113.88/98 from 113.11/10.

The dollar remained somewhat captive to a gyrating stock market for a third straight session, with dollar ups and downs roughly matching the swings in the Dow Jones industrials. The Dow traded sharply lower, then surged back to end almost unchanged.
"The fact that the stock market is ending rather neutral is helping the dollar. When it was off earlier today, the dollar was pressing its lows against European currencies," Ullrich said.
The dollar has been dragged lower over the past two trading days by heavy losses in U.S. stock markets.
Against the Swiss franc, the greenback rallied after an earlier sell-off after Swiss National Bank member Bruno Gehrig said the Swiss franc was no longer clearly overvalued.
In other trading, the dollar closed rose to 1.3240/50 Swiss francs compared to 1.3070/80 francs and to Canadian $1.3628/33 from C$1.3602/07. Sterling fell slightly to $1.6557/67 from $1.6580/90.
The Australian dollar ended off at $0.7915/20 from $0.7925/30.
